text:
Alex Rivera: Heads-up — I want to propose a change to our runtime flag targeting model: make targeting shard-aware and introduce a small typed schema for targeting criteria. we need to avoid breaking existing behavior for Dedicated/Private.
Priya Shah: Can you sketch the failure mode? is this about uneven load after rolling out a new quantization profile?
Alex Rivera: Kinda. Today some flags are percentage-only which rips through routes unpredictably. Shard-aware targeting (hash(route_id) % N) would let us do predictable per-route rollouts and safe canaries.
Mateo Cruz: I like deterministic rollouts. Concern: telemetry naming. if we flip schema we must tag metrics with schema_version otherwise historic comparisons break.
Jordan Li: +1. Proposal: keep current API but accept an optional "targeting_schema_version" header/field. default to v1. we add v2 that supports shard keys + operator lists.
Emma Novak: Console UX needs a preview: show top-10 affected routes and estimated token delta before commit. ops will want an "impact estimate" checkbox.
Priya Shah: Also need per-tenant override for Private deployments. they might run older agents that don't understand v2. backcompat is critical.
Alex Rivera: Agreed. Migration plan sketch:
- step 1: add v2 schema to API, default behavior remains v1
- step 2: add server-side opt-in flag: admin.enable_v2_targeting (off by default)
- step 3: console preview + dry-run (no effect) to compute impacted routes
- step 4: canary rollout via config: target specific shards/customer ids
Mateo Cruz: For telemetry, let's emit a one-off event: config.change.v2 with fields: who, dry_run:true/false, sample_routes: [..]. Also stamp each rollout with rollout_id.
SREBot: deploy-bot: new config service has been deployed to staging at 2026-03-20T15:04:12Z (build rfd-targeting-3a). Logs: /var/log/deploys/targeting-3a.log
Jordan Li: Implementation detail: we should reuse our existing hash function (consistent across runtime variants). don't invent a new sharding function.
Emma Novak: UX note: add a toggle in the rollout modal "deterministic shard targeting" with an info tooltip and a link to the RFC.
Priya Shah: API example for admin patch (dry-run):
```
curl -X PATCH "https://admin.redwood.internal/flags/targeting" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"schema_version":"v2","dry_run":true,"rules":[{"shard_key":"route_id","percent":10}] }'
```
Mateo Cruz: Good. Also ensure the evaluation path returns a structured diff so console can render it.
Alex Rivera: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with migration details, telemetry fields, and an ops rollback playbook. tagging folks: @Priya @Mateo @Jordan @Emma — add anything else you want in the RFC.
Priya Shah: Add a section on ALB/circuit-breaker interaction and cost estimate (token delta) for large customers.
Jordan Li: Add tests: unit tests for hash edge cases, integration test for v1<->v2 compatibility.
Emma Novak: I'll mock the console preview and attach screenshots to the RFC.
Mateo Cruz: And let's schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow. I'll bring historical incident examples where percentage-only caused noisy failures.
Alex Rivera: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC link here once ready. :thumbsup:
